name: Egyptian Revival

revival_periods.note: The Tutankhamun discovery of November 1922 produced a second and entirely different Egyptomania, absorbed into Art Deco and into cinema architecture rather than into a traditional building grammar.

lineage.note: The same architects (Strickland, Haviland, Austin, Lafever), the same masons, the same archaeological method, the same trabeated discipline. Egyptian Revival is Greek Revival practice pointed at a different corpus of plates.
Only through the Roman appetite for Egyptian spolia and the obelisk, which reached the nineteenth century as an inherited funerary sign.
In the cemetery-gate debate of the 1840s the Egyptian mode was argued for and against precisely as the pagan alternative to the Christian pointed arch; the two competed for the same commissions.

description.short: A narrow, short-lived, and almost entirely institutional American style of battered walls, cavetto cornices, and lotus columns, adopted for prisons, cemeteries, medical colleges, and a handful of churches because it read as permanent, solemn, and pre-Christian.
description.long:
Egyptian Revival is the smallest node in this branch and the one that best exposes how nineteenth-century Americans actually chose styles: by association, deliberately and almost semiotically. Napoleon's savants published the Description de l'Egypte between 1809 and 1829 and Dominique-Vivant Denon's Voyage dans la Basse et la Haute Egypte appeared in 1802, and within a generation American architects had a picture book of a civilisation whose buildings were understood to be the oldest and most durable on earth. That association, permanence beyond memory, made the mode almost irresistible for two building types: the cemetery, where the client wants to promise that the dead will not be disturbed, and the prison, where the client wants to promise that the living will not escape. It was used for both, and almost never for a house.

The style is trabeated, frontal, and massive. Walls batter inward as they rise; every terminating edge is turned with a torus roll and crowned by a cavetto cornice; columns are bundled reeds or papyrus stalks with lotus or palm capitals, squat and closely spaced; openings are small and rectangular; the winged sun disk sits over the door. Because the sources were engravings of temples rather than of dwellings, there was no domestic vocabulary to borrow, and the mode never developed one. This is a structural fact about revivalism worth recording in a taxonomy: a revival can only supply the building types its source corpus documented.

Its technological position is the mirror image of the rest of this branch. Egyptian Revival is a masonry style in an era that was learning to build cheaply in light wood, and it is precisely that mismatch which confined it. You cannot batter a balloon-framed wall convincingly, you cannot saw a torus moulding from a plank, and a cavetto cornice is a mason's or a plasterer's problem, not a millwright's. Where Gothic and Italianate detail rode the scroll saw and the railroad into every county in America, Egyptian detail stayed where there were stonecutters and institutional budgets. The Egyptian Building in Richmond gets its effect from stuccoed brick and cast iron; the Grove Street gate in New Haven from Portland sandstone. Both are the work of trades that were already being priced out of ordinary building.

Standing in front of one is genuinely unlike standing in front of any other American building of the period. Because the walls lean back, the building appears to be receding from you and settling into the ground at the same time, and because the cornice curves outward rather than stepping outward, the top of the wall reads as a lip rather than as a crown. There is no entasis to sympathise with, no bracket rhythm to follow, no order to measure yourself against. The effect is deliberately inhuman in scale reference, and everyone who commissioned one understood that. It is the only American traditional style whose purpose is to make the viewer feel small and temporary.

defining_characteristics: Battered (inward-sloping) exterior walls, typically 1:12 to 1:20 from vertical
Cavetto (hollow curved) cornice with a torus roll moulding at every terminating edge
Columns of bundled-reed or papyrus form with lotus or palm capitals, squat in proportion and never fluted
Trabeated openings throughout: post and lintel, no arches of any kind
Battered pylon forms flanking the principal entrance
Winged sun disk, vulture, or uraeus ornament placed in the cavetto over the entry
Massive, unbroken, minimally fenestrated wall surface
diagnostic_tells: Walls that lean inward as they rise: no other nineteenth-century American style batters its walls
The cornice curves outward in a concave sweep rather than stepping out in mouldings; this alone identifies the style at a hundred yards
Columns are wider at the base than a Greek Doric and shorter, typically four to five diameters, and stand in antis between battered piers rather than in a projecting portico
The building will almost certainly be a cemetery gate, a prison, a medical or scientific institution, a synagogue, or a church; a domestic Egyptian Revival is vanishingly rare
Obelisks used as gateposts, terminals, or fence standards

distinguished_from.difference: Shared architects and shared archaeology, opposite geometry. Greek Revival walls are plumb, its columns are slender and fluted with entasis, and it terminates in a horizontal entablature and a pediment; Egyptian Revival batters its walls, squats its columns, and terminates in a cavetto with no pediment ever.
Both use heavy masonry and small openings, but Richardsonian is arcuated, rock-faced, and asymmetrical, and Egyptian Revival is trabeated, smooth-faced or stuccoed, and rigidly frontal.

proportional_system.governing_logic: Trabeated and archaeological. Proportions are copied from published plates of Dendera, Edfu, and Philae rather than derived from a module; the governing decisions are the wall batter and the column diameter, and the rest follows the source engraving.
typical_ratios: Wall batter 1:12 to 1:20 (roughly 3 to 5 degrees from vertical)
Column height 4 to 5.5 shaft diameters, the squattest proportion in any Western revival
Cavetto cornice height 0.8 to 1.2 times the torus roll diameter times six
Window area not exceeding 20 percent of any elevation
proportional_system.bay_rhythm: Frontal and centralised: a heavy pylon or portico at the centre, flanked by near-blank battered wall. The rhythm is A-B-A, never a repeating march of equal bays.

massing_affinities.note: In the Egyptian variant the centre is distyle in antis between battered piers rather than a pedimented portico.
The rare domestic or institutional block, battered on all four faces.
Picturesque irregularity is incompatible with a frontal, symmetrical, mass-dominated style.

constraints.statement: All principal exterior walls shall batter inward between 1:12 and 1:20 from base to cornice. A plumb-walled building with Egyptian ornament is not Egyptian Revival.

Every terminating horizontal edge shall be composed as torus roll below cavetto cornice, in that order and without intervening classical mouldings. Dentils, modillions, and egg-and-dart are forbidden anywhere on the building.
No arches. All openings shall be spanned by lintels. A single round or pointed arch voids the identification.

test.note: A zero-rise head over every opening is the geometric signature of a flat lintel span with no arch, so the statement's own 'no arches, all openings spanned by lintels' is captured using the existing arch-rise variable at zero rather than an arch-presence boolean the vocabulary doesn't have.

constraints.statement: Column shaft height shall be between 4 and 5.5 base diameters, with intercolumniation between 1.5 and 2.5 diameters. Shafts shall be reed-bundle or palm form and shall never carry classical fluting or entasis.

The winged sun disk shall appear once per elevation, in the cavetto directly over the principal entry. Repeating it along a frieze is a twentieth-century cinema convention, not a nineteenth-century one.

exemplars.name: Egyptian Building, Medical College of Virginia
exemplars.note: Thomas S. Stewart. Battered walls, distyle in antis porticoes with palm capitals, flanking obelisks joined by a cast-iron fence with hermai. The finest surviving American example and still in university use.

exemplars.name: Grove Street Cemetery Gateway
exemplars.note: Henry Austin, 1845-48. Red sandstone, two battered pylons with torus framing and cavetto cornice, about 48 ft wide by 25 ft high.

exemplars.name: Downtown Presbyterian Church
exemplars.note: William Strickland, designed 1848, sanctuary completed 1851. Lotus columns, winged sun disk, and a fully Egyptianised interior; the rare ecclesiastical case.

sources: Richard G. Carrott, The Egyptian Revival: Its Sources, Monuments and Meaning, 1808-1858 (1978)
Marcus Whiffen, American Architecture Since 1780: A Guide to the Styles (1969)
James Stevens Curl, The Egyptian Revival (2005)
Society of Architectural Historians, SAH Archipedia entries for the Egyptian Building and Grove Street Cemetery Gate

proportion_packs.note:
SCOPED BINDING (OQ 49), AND IT TAKES THE CORPUS TO 132 OF 132. This was the one deliberately unbound buildable node: WP-4.1 held it out because nothing fitted its trabeated order and recorded that naming the gap beat forcing a pack onto it, and WP-4.6 confirmed the judgment from the other side -- two of `facade-peristyle`'s rules fit exactly and thirteen do not.

The distinction from the thing WP-4.1 refused matters and is not a technicality. Binding the whole pack would have handed this node a peristyle count it has no peristyle for, a Vitruvian column-height function, a stylobate curvature, a corner contraction and an ENTASIS -- which its own c04 forbids outright, 'shafts shall be reed-bundle or palm form and shall never carry classical fluting or entasis'. The scope admits two rules and excludes those, including the one the node prohibits.

`column/front_count`: distyle in antis is 2, the floor of the pack's 2-to-8 band, and the node's own bay rhythm is 'A-B-A, never a repeating march of equal bays', which is why the peristyle rules are excluded rather than merely unused. `column/intercolumniation_roman`: the node gives 1.5 to 2.5 diameters, 'notably tight', which sits inside the pack's 1.5-to-4.0 band. THE DIMENSION IS NAMED `roman` BECAUSE ROME GENERATED THE BAND, not because this is Roman work, and the pack supplies the quantity and its units while the node's own narrower figure governs. What is NOT claimed: no column height, because the pack's only height rule is Vitruvius's function and this node's 4-to-5.5 diameters is archaeological rather than derived -- and squatter than anything in the pack except Archaic Doric at 4.3, which its own record does not notice.

declined_packs.reason: The pack's own notes make its subject a complete Grecian Doric order and list the five things it does that no Roman order does: no base, seven diameters, an entablature of two, a continuous entasis with no cylindrical lower portion at all, and flutes segmental in wood. The node's c04 forbids the last two outright, and its typical_ratios put the shaft at 4 to 5.5 diameters, the squattest proportion in any Western revival -- the order's own governing figures contradicted, not merely varied. Its distinguished_from entry says the same thing from the other side about the slot the pack actually governs here: Greek Revival 'terminates in a horizontal entablature and a pediment; Egyptian Revival ... terminates in a cavetto with no pediment ever'. This is the pack's stated subject being refused by the node's own record, not an inference from the pack's name or from the ancestor it arrived on.
declined_packs.quote: Shafts shall be reed-bundle or palm form and shall never carry classical fluting or entasis
declined_packs.note: Governs 2 slots (cornice, pilaster); declining hands both to benjamin-ionic delivered from federal-style, and 0 slots lose all dimensioning. Honest consequence: the decline stops the Grecian Doric authority but its successor is another classical order, because no Egyptian pack exists to take a cavetto cornice -- the slot stays wrongly dimensioned by a different hand.

declined_packs.reason: The pack's notes make its subject Vignola's Ionic in full -- the 18-part module, the fluted shaft of 18 modules, the frontal volute capital drawn from twelve centres, and an entablature it subdivides down to individual mouldings -- and one of the twelve slots it dimensions is literally modillion_dentil. The node's c02 forbids dentils, modillions and egg-and-dart anywhere on the building and requires every terminating horizontal edge to be torus roll below cavetto without intervening classical mouldings; its defining characteristics give columns of bundled-reed or papyrus form with lotus or palm capitals, never fluted. Each of the pack's stated subjects -- the capital, the shaft, the entablature's mouldings -- is named and refused by a sentence of the node's own record.
declined_packs.quote: Dentils, modillions, and egg-and-dart are forbidden anywhere on the building.
declined_packs.note: Governs 0 slots on this node, so declining changes no dimension: the --impact report says so in as many words. The meter moves and nothing else does.

declined_packs.reason: The pack's own notes state its subject as Benjamin's Federal Roman Ionic taken as a delta on Vignola -- 'everything not stated here is Vignola's' -- and the third of the five divergences it names is 'THE CORNICE CARRIES MODILLIONS', at 31 minutes on centres, each centred on a column, with a dentilled cornice offered as the alternative. Both of the pack's own offered cornices are named and forbidden by this node's c02, which also requires every terminating horizontal edge to be torus roll below cavetto 'without intervening classical mouldings'. That is the pack's stated subject refused by a sentence of the node's own record, not an inference from the pack's name; it is also the same ground on which this node already declined `vignola-ionic`, the pack this one overlays. The cornice slot the pack governs here is precisely the edge the node's own tell says 'curves outward in a concave sweep rather than stepping out in mouldings'.

declined_packs.note: Governs 3 slots (cornice, door_surround, pilaster); declining hands all three to gibbs-ionic delivered from georgian-colonial-american, and 0 slots lose all dimensioning. Honest consequence, and it is the same one recorded for benjamin-doric: the decline stops the Federal Ionic authority but its successor is another classical order, because no Egyptian pack exists to take a cavetto cornice -- the slot stays wrongly dimensioned by a different hand.

declined_packs.reason: The pack's own notes state its subject as the archaeological Greek Doric order measured by Stuart and Revett -- the column in diameters, the Doric entablature and its mutules per triglyph interval, and an ornament vocabulary stated at zero -- and say explicitly that it dimensions the order rather than a temple front. The node's own diagnostic tell names Greek Doric directly and states that its columns differ from it in both diameter and height, and its c04 forbids the fluting and entasis that the pack's notes discuss as the order's own corrected properties. The headline figure is the trap here and is not the reason: the pack's 5.5 diameters coincides with the top of this node's 4-to-5.5 band, and the node's record says in as many words that its columns are shorter than a Greek Doric's. Coincidence of a number, contradiction of the mechanism.

It dimensions cornice, crown, entablature, frieze, casing, chair_rail, porch_support, ornament_vocabulary and, literally, modillion_dentil. The node's c02 forbids dentils, modillions and egg-and-dart anywhere on the building and requires every terminating horizontal edge to be composed as torus roll below cavetto without intervening classical mouldings, and its second tell says the cornice curves outward in a concave sweep rather than stepping out in mouldings. c04 puts the shaft at 4 to 5.5 base diameters against the pack's eleven and forbids classical fluting and entasis outright. DIRECTION CHECK: the node's column is SHORTER than the order's, so the contradiction is of the order's own governing figure and is read the right way round. Same ground as the node's existing vignola-ionic and benjamin-ionic declines.

declined_packs.reason: The pack's own notes state its subject as Gibbs's Ionic as a delta on Vignola, headed by the entablature at one fifth of the column, and the second of its named divergences is the cornice: 'Gibbs's principal Ionic cornice carries modillions at three quarters of a diameter on centres; Vignola's carries dentils and no modillions. Gibbs offers a dentil version as the alternative'. BOTH of the pack's offered cornices are named and forbidden by this node's c02, which also requires every terminating horizontal edge to be torus roll below cavetto without intervening classical mouldings -- the identical finding already recorded on this node against benjamin-ionic, whose decline note says its three slots would pass to gibbs-ionic, which is how this gap arose. On this node the pack governs cornice, door_surround, eave_condition and pilaster, which is precisely the terminating edge c02 composes. c04 independently puts the shaft at 4 to 5.5 base diameters, against an Ionic order of nine and more, and forbids classical fluting and entasis; the second tell says the cornice sweeps concave rather than stepping out in mouldings.
declined_packs.quote: Dentils, modillions, and egg-and-dart are forbidden anywhere on the building.
declined_packs.note: Arrives from georgian-colonial-american at cascade depth 5 with no direct lineage edge. THE GATE: gibbs-ionic's applies_to IS a live gate -- build/elevation.py:1429 reads `style in gibbs_pack.get('applies_to', [])` to publish gibbs_order_applies_to_style and to drop the note_order_not_named_for_style disclosure -- but this verdict goes the other way, and a decline writes declined_packs without touching applies_to, so the gate is untouched by it. `choose_pack` returns it on 4 slots, which is not the same as the pack emitting a rule for 4: it emits none for eave_condition at all. THE DECLINE IS EFFECTIVE ON THREE -- cornice, door_surround and pilaster, all to chambers-ionic (english-georgian), 0 losing dimensioning, the successor being another classical order, which is OQ 58's stated limit. IT IS NOT EFFECTIVE ON eave_condition: the resolved record there, inherited whole from georgian-colonial-american, carries a slot-level `packs` block naming gibbs-ionic at precedence 1 with its own expression `storey_height / 4 * (7 / 18)`, and `choose_pack` ranks that block above the rows, so dropping the pack from the cascade cannot touch it. Nothing in the generator evaluates that expression today -- `pack_choice` has one producer and no consumer, reaching users only as passthrough through `tdl_resolve_kit` -- so it is a stale ruling served to a reader, not a wrong figure on a sheet. That address stays UNJUDGED by this decline. It is OQ 87's mechanism and a fresh instance of `oq/a-baked-pack-value-is-a-second-delivery-path` in an inherited `slot.packs` block rather than a baked kit parameter; `--impact` now says so in words rather than printing `(None)`.
